business_summary: India's second-largest credit-card issuer by cards in force (HDFC Bank leads; SBI 'retains' debit-card share 25%), ~69% owned by State Bank of India (model knowledge). Earns interest on revolving/EMI receivables (~Rs58k cr, -2% YoY), interchange and fees on ~Rs1.1 lakh cr quarterly spends, plus insurance/other. Q2 FY27 PAT Rs778cr (+75%) on lower credit costs (impairments -37% to Rs819cr), revenue only +3-4%; credit cost 5.6%. Stock Rs580.6, -34% in 12m; analysts flag margin pressure from the shift to EMI loans (ET BFSI, JPMorgan, Nuvama).

exposures.mechanism: +50bp credit cost on receivables Rs58.4k cr = Rs292cr pre-tax = Rs219cr post-tax vs run-rate PAT ~Rs3,100cr (Q2 x4) => -7% PAT; cycle persistence 0.5 => -3.5. Credit cost already fell to 5.6% (guide ~6% FY27), so downside is from a reversal.

evidence.note: SBI Card Q2 FY27 PAT Rs778cr (+75%), impairments -37% to Rs819cr, receivables Rs58,376cr (-2% YoY), retail spends Rs95,299cr (+6%), credit cost 5.6% vs 6.5% in Q1; FY27 credit-cost guide ~6% (search summaries, psuconnect/Multibagg/Business Standard)

exposures.mechanism: +1pp card delinquencies (cards are 100% unsecured) = ~+1pp credit cost = Rs584cr pre-tax = Rs437cr post-tax = -14% of run-rate PAT; persistence 0.45 (reverts within ~3 quarters) => -6. This was the driver of the 2024-26 drawdown and the 75% PAT rebound in Q2 FY27 was entirely from lower credit costs (impairments -37%).

+5pp urban consumption growth => card spends +6% (spends Rs1.1 lakh cr/qtr; retail Rs95.3k cr, +6% YoY) => interchange/fee income +4%, receivables +3% => PAT +5% x persistence 0.7 => +3.5. Spends are growing only 3-6% now, so there is room for upside.
